provenance.orgName: Reading, Berkshire, Benedictine abbey of Saint Mary the Virgin
provenance.p: This attribution was rejected in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964), which did not change in the Supplement (1987). The corresponding Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card records no further context for the rejection.

Compare the following discussion from Vivien Law and James P. Carley, ‘Grammar and Arithmetic in Two Thirteenth-Century English Monastic Collections: Cambridge, Sidney Sussex College, MS 75 and Oxford, Bodleian Library, MS Bodley 186 (S.C. 2088)’, Journal of Medieval Latin, 1 (1991), 146: "[Bodley MS 186] is ... one of a group of thirty-one manuscripts given to Sir Thomas Bodley by William Burdett of Sonning in 1608. Of these manuscripts twenty can be shown on internal grounds to be Reading manuscripts and Liddell was tempted to attribute nine more -- of which [Bodley MS 186] is one -- to the same source, even though there is no conclusive proof of the provenances for these nine; hence Ker's subsequent rejection. Here the matter has rested ever since. Some jottings in medieval hands on a front flyleaf of [Bodley MS 186], hitherto overlooked, offer valuable corroborative evidence for Liddell's assumption. One of them, in a late fifteenth-century hand, gives the name "Clemens Braye." Now, one Clement Braye, a monk of Reading, participated in the election of John Thome II as abbot in 1486, and one can postulate, therefore, that this represents his signature. [Bodley MS 186], then, must have been at Reading in the late fifteenth century when Clement Braye scribbled in it ...".
